original_question: Can the structure theorem proved for smooth projective varieties with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature, including the locally trivial MRC fibration and the splitting description of the universal cover, be generalized to compact Kahler manifolds?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.5, stated immediately after Theorem 3.4 (= [39, Theorem 1.3]): "Can we generalize Theorem 3.4 to compact Kähler manifolds?" This is the nearest official formulation of the draft. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the relevant section of the paper: it is about the structure theorem for smooth projective varieties with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature, and it singles out two of the theorem's headline conclusions, namely the locally trivial MRC fibration and the universal-cover splitting. It also correctly captures that the paper's open problem is to extend this package from the smooth projective case to the compact Kähler case. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
missing_details: The hypothesis should be stated as a complex-geometric pair (X, g), where X is a compact Kähler manifold and g is a Kähler metric on X whose holomorphic sectional curvature is semi-positive; the draft mentions the manifold class but not the metric data. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The source result being generalized is specifically Theorem 3.4 of this paper, which is the restatement of [39, Theorem 1.3]; naming that theorem makes the question paper-faithful and avoids sounding broader than intended. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The theorem is not merely about an abstract 'structure'; it asserts the existence of a surjective morphism phi: X -> Y, and the local triviality is a property of this morphism. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The flatness of the base is part of the theorem: in the projective case, Y carries a flat metric and admits a finite étale cover A -> Y by an abelian variety. The draft omits this base-side conclusion. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The fiber conclusion should be stated explicitly: the fiber F is rationally connected, and therefore phi is an MRC fibration. Also, 'MRC' should be expanded once as 'maximal rationally connected'. Section 2 gives the precise projective definition of an MRC fibration. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The universal-cover statement is more specific than a generic 'splitting description': X_univ is biholomorphic to C^m x F, where m = dim Y, and there is a representation rho: pi_1(Y) -> Aut(F) such that X is isomorphic to (C^m x F)/pi_1(Y). ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The theorem also includes the induced fundamental-group statement, namely that pi_1(X) is an extension of a finite group by Z^{2m}, which the draft leaves implicit. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The metric part of the theorem is also omitted in the draft: there exist Kähler metrics g_F on F and g_Y on Y with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature on F, flatness on Y, and an isometric product splitting on the universal cover. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The nearby context sharpens the intended compact-Kähler version via Problem 3.6 and Problem 3.3: one should also keep in view the Albanese-map approach, the expected projectivity/rational connectedness of the fiber, and the role of the fundamental group. These are not equivalent reformulations, but they explain what the paper means by a compact-Kähler generalization of Theorem 3.4. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
refined_question: Let (X, g) be a compact Kähler manifold over C with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Does the full analogue of Theorem 3.4 hold for (X, g)? Equivalently in expanded form: must there exist a surjective locally trivial holomorphic map phi: X -> Y that serves as a maximal rationally connected (MRC) fibration, with rationally connected fiber F and flat base Y, such that X_univ is biholomorphic to C^m x F for m = dim Y, X is obtained from this product via a representation rho: pi_1(Y) -> Aut(F), and the corresponding fundamental-group and metric-splitting conclusions of Theorem 3.4 also remain valid in the compact Kähler setting? ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Section 3, Problem 3.5. That problem is posed immediately after Theorem 3.4, and Theorem 3.4 is exactly the result whose contents the draft alludes to: a locally trivial MRC fibration, a flat base after finite étale cover by an abelian variety, a rationally connected fiber, the universal-cover product decomposition, a quotient description via a representation of the fundamental group, and metric/fundamental-group consequences. The follow-up discussion in Problem 3.6 and the reference back to Problem 3.3 show that the paper's intent is the compact-Kähler extension of this precise theorem, not a broader neighboring question. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
